glossaryPage.label: Glossary
glossaryPage.title: 7aychain Terminology
glossaryPage.description: Key terms, modules, and concepts in the 7aychain Proof of Presence protocol — from witness circles to ZK circuits.

autonomousDetection.definition: An on-chain module that automatically flags suspicious patterns in presence verifications. Detects coordinated bot behavior, spoofed timing, and statistical outliers without manual reports.

boomerangProof.definition: A cryptographic proof that someone returned to a previously verified location. Proves consistent presence patterns over time without revealing the location — enabling reputation without surveillance.

circuitRegistry.definition: The on-chain registry of ZK circuits available for proof generation and verification. Manages circuit versions, proof mode migration, and verifier configurations.

commitRevealScheme.definition: A two-phase anti-tampering protocol: first commit a hash of your presence data (hiding it), then reveal the actual data in a later phase. Prevents front-running and ensures fair ordering.

deviceScanner.definition: A module for registering devices that participate in presence verification. Manages device identity, verification capability, and revocation — ensuring only authorized hardware contributes.

disputeResolution.definition: The on-chain process for challenging presence verifications. Disputants submit cryptographic evidence, validators vote, and the protocol enforces outcomes — including slashing for dishonest verifiers.

epoch.definition: A fixed time window during which presence declarations and verifications occur. Epochs structure the protocol lifecycle, determine validator rotation, and isolate verification rounds.

groth16.definition: A zero-knowledge proof system used by 7aychain for compact, non-interactive presence proofs. Delivers constant-size proofs with fast on-chain verification — critical for scalable privacy.

laudNetworksCli.definition: A Python-based terminal interface for interacting with all 16 7aychain modules. Supports presence declaration, validator management, ZK proofs, governance, vaults, and more.

lifecycle.definition: The six-state machine governing a presence declaration: Declare, Commit, Reveal, Attest, Triangulate, and Finalize. Each transition is enforced by the protocol.

multilateration.definition: A positioning technique that estimates physical location from network timing measurements taken at multiple validator points. The core triangulation algorithm powering witness circles.

octopusGroups.definition: Organizational units that group validators and participants for coordinated presence operations. Groups can define shared governance rules and collective verification thresholds.

positionBoundToken.definition: A token minted when presence is verified. PBTs bind verification claims to specific positions and time windows, serving as proof-of-presence credentials — without revealing exact locations.

presenceLifecycle.definition: The six-phase protocol flow: Declare (announce intent), Commit (submit hash), Reveal (disclose data), Attest (validators measure), Triangulate (compute position), Finalize (quorum seal).

proofOfPresence.definition: 7aychain's consensus mechanism. Validators form witness circles and verify physical presence through network timing measurement — no GPS, no biometrics, no external hardware. Bot-proof by design.

quorumConsensus.definition: The validator agreement threshold required to finalize a presence verification. A declaration is only finalized when enough validators in the witness circle converge on a position estimate.

semanticLinks.definition: On-chain relationships between entities (people, locations, organizations) forming a trust graph. Enable contextual verification and reputation scoring based on verified presence history.

shamirSecretSharing.definition: A cryptographic scheme used in 7aychain's vault system to split sensitive data across multiple parties. No single party holds enough to reconstruct the secret — enabling secure recovery without central custody.

snark.definition: Succinct Non-interactive Argument of Knowledge. A zero-knowledge proof type used by 7aychain for compact, efficiently verifiable presence proofs.

storageLayer.definition: A module providing on-chain and off-chain data storage for presence proofs, verification records, and protocol state. Supports pinning, retrieval, and data availability guarantees.

triangulation.definition: The process by which validators estimate physical position using network timing measurements from multiple reference points. Combines multilateration with position algorithms for high-confidence verification.

validator.definition: A node operator who stakes $7AY to participate in consensus, presence verification, and witness circle triangulation. Earns rewards for honest behavior; faces slashing for dishonesty.

vault.definition: A secure on-chain storage system using Shamir secret sharing for distributed key management. Enables data recovery and controlled sharing — without central custody.

witnessCircle.definition: A randomly selected group of validators assigned to verify a presence claim. Circle members independently measure timing and collectively confirm the person's physical position.

zkCircuit.definition: A zero-knowledge computation circuit that generates proofs verifying presence without revealing exact location data. 7aychain uses Groth16 circuits with an on-chain registry.

whyPresencePage.label: Why Presence
whyPresencePage.title: The Internet Lost the Human Signal
whyPresencePage.description: When bots can replicate everything humans do online, the only unforgeable proof left is physical presence.

presenceInfrastructure.paragraph1: At the heart of 7aychain is a simple idea: your internet connection can prove where you are. Validators across the network measure connection timing from multiple points, confirming physical location without GPS, cameras, or special hardware.
presenceInfrastructure.paragraph2: Most identity systems rely on behavior, accounts, or credentials. At scale, all can be faked. 7aychain takes a fundamentally different approach: it uses the laws of physics.

physicsArgument.label: The Physics Argument
physicsArgument.title: Bot resistance through physical reality
physicsArgument.subtitle: Instead of trusting profiles, credentials, or biometrics, 7aychain exploits a fundamental constraint: you can only be in one place at a time.

0.title: Physics, Not Scans
0.description: Internet signals obey the speed of light. 7aychain uses this to confirm where you are. No iris scans. No selfies. No fingerprints.

1.title: One Place at a Time
1.description: Create a million wallets — you can still only be in one physical location. That constraint makes bot attacks nearly impossible.

2.title: No Lasting Footprint
2.description: Each verification is ephemeral. No persistent profile, no behavioral tracking, no stored data. Prove you were here, then it's done.

coreInsight.label: Core Insight
coreInsight.title: In a world of perfect simulation, physical reality is the scarce resource
coreInsight.description: AI generates convincing text, behavior, and interaction at scale. But physical presence — being at a specific place at a specific time, measurable through network physics — remains constrained by natural law.

0.response: AI fakes text, transactions, and social activity. It can't fake being somewhere. Physical presence is bound by the laws of physics.

1.response: New wallets cost nothing. Being in two places at once is impossible. 7aychain turns a digital problem into a physical constraint.

2.response: Iris scans and facial recognition create permanent databases of your body. 7aychain measures connection timing — it never sees your face or knows your name.

3.response: Coordinated groups fabricate social proof. Physical presence is independently verified by the network — no trust assumptions needed.

validatorsPage.description: Earn $7AY rewards by securing the network. Validators form witness circles, verify physical presence, and keep the protocol honest.

roleOverview.label: Role Overview
roleOverview.title: What validators do
roleOverview.paragraph1: On 7aychain, validators do more than produce blocks. They actively verify that people are where they claim to be — forming witness circles that confirm each person's location through network timing measurement.
roleOverview.paragraph2: Each validator in a witness circle measures round-trip timing to the declaring participant and to other validators. These measurements feed into position algorithms that determine physical location — without GPS or external hardware.
roleOverview.paragraph3: When enough validators agree on a position, the presence is confirmed and permanently sealed on-chain. Honest validators earn $7AY rewards. Dishonest ones get slashed.
roleOverview.paragraph4: The validator set rotates each round, preventing any single group from colluding to falsify presence verifications.

witnessCircles.label: Protocol
witnessCircles.title: Witness circle participation
witnessCircles.paragraph1: When someone declares presence, the protocol selects a group of active validators to form a
witnessCircles.paragraph1cont: . Selection is random, weighted by stake and shaped by network topology.
witnessCircles.paragraph2: Each validator in the circle independently measures round-trip timing to the declaring participant and to other circle members. These measurements are submitted as signed verifications.

witnessCircles.paragraph4: If the position estimate from enough validators converges within threshold, the presence is finalized. Outlier measurements trigger dispute resolution, and validators providing false verifications face slashing.

2.title: 7aychain v0.8.26 released
2.summary: Latest stable release with the complete Proof of Presence protocol stack.
2.content: Released 7aychain v0.8.26 — the latest stable version of the Layer 1 blockchain. Includes the complete protocol stack: presence lifecycle with commit-reveal, witness-circle triangulation, ZK proof verification, validator staking/slashing, governance, vaults, semantic linking, dispute resolution, device scanning, and autonomous detection. Multi-node devnet running with 6 validators.

3.title: Governance and vault system shipped
3.summary: On-chain governance with proposals and voting, plus secure vault infrastructure.
3.content: Shipped on-chain governance with proposals, voting, and delegation. Implemented the vault system with create, share, recover, register-file, request-unlock, and authorize-unlock operations. Added semantic linking for trust graphs between on-chain entities.

4.title: ZK circuits and triangulation integrated
4.summary: Zero-knowledge proofs and position algorithms now live on devnet.
4.content: Integrated ZK proof generation and on-chain verification for privacy-preserving presence verification. Implemented position algorithms that determine location from network timing measurements without GPS. Added position-bound tokens (PBTs) for cryptographic position claims.

5.title: Validator system and dispute resolution
5.summary: Complete validator lifecycle: registration, staking, slashing, and disputes.
5.content: Implemented the complete validator system: registration, activation, deactivation, withdrawal, staking, and slashing. Added dispute resolution with evidence submission, voting, and on-chain enforcement. Validators form witness circles and participate in quorum-based presence finalization.

6.title: Multi-node devnet and CLI launched
6.summary: Hybrid devnet with 6 validators and Laud Networks CLI for full protocol interaction.
6.content: Launched multi-node hybrid devnet with Alice running natively and remaining validators (Bob, Charlie, Dave, Eve, Ferdie) in Docker. Released the Laud Networks CLI with interactive commands for all protocol modules.

7.title: Presence and epoch core shipped
7.summary: Foundational presence lifecycle and time-window management — the protocol backbone.
7.content: Built the core presence state machine (Declared, Attested, Triangulated, Finalized) with time-bound lifecycle. Implemented dynamic state derivation from block timestamps. Established participant isolation and authority-controlled state transitions.

8.title: Problem validation complete
8.summary: Validated core problem with early teams across events, communities, and logistics.
8.content: Validated core problem with early teams. Conducted structured interviews and research across event organizers, community builders, and logistics operators. Confirmed that presence verification is a high-pain, low-solution problem space.

description.0: We started 7ayLabs with one question: what if you could prove you were somewhere without revealing who you are?
description.1: That question became 7aychain — an L1 that verifies presence using the physics of the internet itself.

mission.label: What We're Building
mission.title: Our Mission
mission.paragraph1: 7ayLabs builds 7aychain — a new kind of Layer 1. Instead of scanning your eyes or demanding ID, the network verifies you're physically present using nothing more than your internet connection.
mission.paragraph2: Validators measure connection timing from multiple points to confirm your location. No GPS. No cameras. No special hardware.
mission.paragraph3: In a world where bots are indistinguishable from humans online, presence becomes the most valuable signal. We're building the infrastructure to make that signal available to everyone.
mission.paragraph4: For protocols and DAOs: bot-proof governance, fair airdrops, and a reliable answer to “was this a real person?”
mission.paragraph5: For people: prove you were somewhere without giving up your identity. No surveillance. No data harvesting. Just proof.

vision.label: Our Long-Term View
vision.title: Our Vision
vision.paragraph1: We see a future where “being there” is a first-class digital primitive. As AI perfects simulation, physical presence becomes the one thing that can't be faked.
vision.paragraph2: 7ayLabs is building the infrastructure for that future. Deliberately, rigorously, and with the standards that real-world systems demand.
